title: Deploying
description: Put a project on the internet at a real address: what hosting actually buys you, deploying a static site end to end, what a build step does to your code before it ships, keeping secrets out of production the safe way, and what a custom domain actually costs.

title: When You Need a Backend
description: Know what has to happen on a server and what doesn't: the real difference between client and server, the specific things a browser can never be trusted to do on its own, writing and calling a first real server endpoint, storing data somewhere that survives a restart, and keeping a secret genuinely server-side instead of just hidden.

title: Users and Accounts
description: Understand what letting people log in actually commits you to: what an account genuinely requires of the person building it, never storing a password you don't have to, how a session keeps someone logged in, when to use an existing auth service instead of building one, and what you're now responsible for the moment real people's data is in your database.

title: After Launch
description: Keep a live project working, including when you haven't looked at it for a month: finding out it broke before a user tells you, writing logs that actually help future-you, updating dependencies without breaking everything at once, coming back to your own project cold, and knowing when to actually turn something off.

title: Capstone — Build and Ship Something Real
description: Take an idea of your own from nothing to a deployed, tested, documented project: choosing something you can actually finish, cutting scope until it fits your real capacity, building in stages that each independently work, pushing through the unglamorous last ten percent, and writing about what you built.
